subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should shipped ownerless session rows be denied to plugin-runtime callers immediately, or migrated or repaired before enforcing the new ownership fence?
rationale: The security invariant favors fail-closed behavior, but the PR explicitly changes legacy ownerless-row behavior and current evidence does not establish whether those rows are shipped persistent state requiring a doctor migration or another upgrade path.

options.title: Migrate then enforce
options.body: Add a narrow doctor or storage migration for safely attributable shipped rows, then fail closed for any remaining ownerless rows.

options.title: Accept immediate fail-closed behavior
options.body: Document and explicitly approve that plugin-runtime patches to all existing ownerless rows will stop working after upgrade.

recommendation.title: Migrate then enforce
recommendation.body: Add a narrow doctor or storage migration for safely attributable shipped rows, then fail closed for any remaining ownerless rows.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest history match for the session accessor and SQLite migration boundary where the upgrade policy would be implemented.
